_note: The guided walkthrough's sample piece in this brand (/prism-tutorial, run.sh tutorial). Fictional agency, people and figures.
title: How Cedar Hollow got its afternoons back
prompt: Draft this into a two-page case study sheet for human services program leaders. The agency, people and figures are illustrative. End on a demo invite.

answers.audience: Human services program leaders (directors and supervisors)
answers.images: The sample's Cedar Hollow logo, as the hero image (fictional organization, sample logo)

start: Read the notes and spot what shouldn't go out as written
Look at how the numbers are written in different ways
interview: Pick a different audience to see what it would change
Skip a question: every one is optional
draft: Compare a line of the notes with the same line in the draft
Find where a number in the draft came from in claims.md
proof: Change the headline to "How Cedar Hollow won back its afternoons"
Reply to one of the Check comments
Open the Claims tab and find where 41% came from
design: Drag the caseworker quote above the results chart
Ask for a different icon on one of the problem cards
export: Ask for a print version on white
Say "make the closing card say Book a demo today"
Open the PDF and check every number against the notes
formats: Ask for another format, such as social posts
Make a layout change to one output only, such as the deck's results slide
revise: Say "the 41% should be 38%" and watch it change in every output

more.prompt: Also make a PowerPoint deck from the same words, for a board meeting.
Also make a LinkedIn carousel of the results.
Also make a 15-second animated film of the results for Instagram stories.
Also make two social posts and a story with captions.
Also make an HTML email announcing the case study to partners.
Also make a blog post with a header image.

fixed._note: A fixed draft, proof and layouts, so every run shows the same doc, flags and boards. The writer, reviewer and formatters don't run for these.

expect._note: What the fixed sheet must build to; the tutorial test builds it and checks.
